entities.title: Years are bigint, seconds are bigint rationals
entities.summary: Years and day counts are bigint, and seconds are exact rationals of two bigints in lowest terms.
entities.context: UTV requires arbitrary precision: integers are decimal strings and fractions exact rationals, never floating point or fixed-width integers. JavaScript's number is a double.
entities.decision: Typed values take and return years as bigint (a number argument must be a safe integer). Internally every instant is a Rational {n, d} of bigints, kept in lowest terms with a positive denominator; day arithmetic is on bigint epoch days.
entities.rationale: The README: "Years are bigint" and "All arithmetic is exact: bigint years and days, rational seconds." library-api §1 names bigint for TypeScript.

entities.title: The typed layer calls the JSON layer
entities.summary: Every typed operation builds or holds its value's UTV JSON and calls a 0.2 JSON-layer function on it, rather than re-implementing the arithmetic.
entities.context: 0.3 adds a typed layer over the 0.2 JSON-level everyday API, which the shared fixtures test. library-api §2 says implementations should call the 0.2 functions underneath.
entities.decision: Each typed class holds its frozen UTV JSON; its methods call ops, zones, native, text and the builders, and turn the utv-result/1.0 answer into a plain value (total operations) or an Outcome (partial ones).
entities.rationale: values.ts: "Every operation calls the 0.2 JSON layer underneath, so the typed layer agrees with the fixtures."

entities.title: Private constructors with static factories
entities.summary: Typed classes have private constructors; static of/tryOf factories validate, and module-level factory functions registered by each class's static block let decode build any class.
entities.context: library-api §1 requires types that are valid by construction and immutable, and fromJson and parse must produce any of the classes from JSON.
entities.decision: Constructors are private. of validates and throws a RangeError; tryOf returns an Outcome. Each class's static block registers a factory (newDate, newInstant, …) that decode uses after the JSON layer's readers have checked the value. The JSON is deep-frozen, and the fields behind it are #private (an Interval's start and end are public readonly Bounds).
entities.rationale: CHANGELOG 0.3.0: "Private constructors and static factories (of throws a RangeError, tryOf returns an Outcome)"; values.ts: "Factories for the private constructors, registered by each class's static block."

entities.title: Outcome<T> is a union of classes discriminated on status
entities.summary: The five outcome cases are classes sharing a base with the helpers, and their union narrows on the status string; assertNever makes a switch exhaustive.
entities.context: library-api §3 asks each language for its own exhaustive sum type; for TypeScript a union discriminated on status, handled with switch and a never check.
entities.decision: Unique, Multiple, None, Unsupported and Invalid extend an unexported OutcomeBase that holds uniqueOr, single, toString and toResult; Outcome<T> is their union. assertNever(x: never) fails to type-check when a case is missing, and throws at run time.
entities.rationale: outcome.ts: "Narrow it with switch (o.status) and finish with default: assertNever(o), so that a missing case fails to type-check." typed.test.ts checks with @ts-expect-error that a missing case does not compile.

entities.title: Policies are const objects that are also string-union types
entities.summary: MonthEnd, Gap, Overlap, Truth and Ordering are frozen const objects whose values form a string-union type of the same name, so MonthEnd.Constrain and "constrain" both type-check.
entities.context: library-api §4: policies are typed in every language; Python and TypeScript may also accept the literal strings through a typed parameter. The JSON layer uses the wire strings.
entities.decision: Each vocabulary is `export const X = {…} as const` plus `export type X = (typeof X)[keyof typeof X]`. Weekday is a numeric enum, Monday = 1. ResolutionPolicy is an interface plus a const with Strict, AllCandidates and of.
entities.rationale: outcome.ts: "each is also its own string-union type, so literals are accepted too"; the values pass straight to the JSON layer.

entities.title: Comparison methods and JavaScript's value protocols
entities.summary: Typed values offer compare, isBefore and isAfter instead of operators, equals instead of a hash, toJSON for JSON.stringify, and a Node inspect view.
entities.context: JavaScript has no operator overloading and no hash protocol; library-api §1 says value semantics in JavaScript means equals() plus immutability, and names toJSON() for TypeScript.
entities.decision: Ordered<Self> adds compare(other): -1 | 0 | 1, isBefore and isAfter where the order is defined. TemporalValue provides equals (same class, same canonical JSON), toJSON, toString (the text form) and Symbol.for("nodejs.util.inspect.custom") giving CivilDate(2026-11-05).
entities.rationale: README: "toJSON() the UTV JSON (so JSON.stringify(value) just works), and equals() compares by value. Node's console.log shows CivilDate(2026-11-05)."

entities.title: Native interop bridges Date, not Temporal
entities.summary: The native adapters convert to and from Date, epoch milliseconds and plain {year, month, day} objects; Temporal is not a target.
entities.context: everyday-api, Native interop: each library offers explicit adapters to the language's own types, the caller names the intent, nothing is read in the host's local zone and loss is reported.
entities.decision: fromDate takes an intent ("instant", { offsetSeconds }, { zone, rules }; "local" is refused); toDate, fromEpochMilliseconds, toEpochMilliseconds, fromPlainDate and toPlainDate complete the set. A Date is read only through getTime().
entities.rationale: native.ts: "Temporal would be the natural native target, but it is not available by default in Node 22."

entities.title: No runtime dependencies
entities.summary: The package has no runtime dependencies: its own strict JSON parser, and ambient declarations instead of @types/node.
entities.context: UTV must reject duplicate JSON keys, which JSON.parse silently accepts (keeping the last value). The library needs one Node built-in, readFileSync, to load a rule file.
entities.decision: json.ts is a hand-written parser that rejects duplicate keys (parseStrict). src/node.d.ts declares node:fs readFileSync (and readdirSync, which the tests use), and test/shim.d.ts declares node:test and node:assert/strict, so typescript is the only devDependency.
entities.rationale: json.ts: "Strict JSON parser that rejects duplicate object keys. No runtime dependencies." node.d.ts: "Declared here so the package needs no @types/node." README: "Runtime dependencies: none."
